# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or any wire, so I cannot safely cut anything. I’m asking Mute to consult the manual and coordinate with Deaf to identify the required wire and conditions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information yet. Read the manual and obtain Deaf's report of every colour and marking, then tell me exactly which wire position to cut and when.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still have no tactile information about the bomb and therefore cannot safely cut a wire. I will ask Mute to provide the manual’s rule and coordinate the needed visual report from Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No tactile markings or wire information are available to me. Please relay the manual rule and Deaf's complete report, including display, light, and wire markings.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 2, the green wire.

Deaf reports that wire 2 is green and says to cut it, but I do not yet know whether the manual permits that action. I need Mute’s rule before touching the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: cut wire 2, the green wire. What does the manual say? Confirm whether wire 2 is the required cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture was ? then ?: two, then right. Previous instruction was to cut wire 2, green.

Mute’s gestures apparently communicate “two, then right,” but gestures do not tell me the manual’s rule reliably, and Deaf’s report only identifies wire 2 as green. I still need Mute to state the instruction in speech before cutting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual instruction to me directly. Deaf reports your gestures as two, then right, but I need the exact wire action in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signalled ?, confirming the instruction to cut wire 2, the green wire.

Deaf confirms that Mute’s signal also instructed me to cut wire 2, and Deaf identified wire 2 as green. Both available reports agree, so I will perform that cut.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New bomb state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 already cut, wire 3 red. Do not act until we identify the next instruction.

Wire 2 was accepted and is cut. The new state is display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, and wire 3 red. I will not cut another wire until Mute gives the manual rule for this state and Deaf confirms the required wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="After cutting wire 2, Deaf reports display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, and wire 3 red. Please provide the manual's next instruction and coordinate with Deaf before I act.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 3, the red wire. The mute signalled ?, meaning three.

The current state is display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, and wire 3 red. Deaf reports that Mute’s gesture means wire 3, and the instruction is to cut the red wire. I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New bomb state: display 0, green light, wire 1 yellow; wires 2 and 3 are already cut. Wait for the next instruction.

Wire 3 was accepted and is cut. The new state is display 0 with a green light; wires 2 and 3 are cut, and wire 1 is yellow. No next instruction has arrived, so I will not act.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 1, the yellow wire. The mute signalled ?, meaning one.

The remaining live wire is wire 1, which Deaf identifies as yellow. Deaf also reports that Mute’s signal means wire 1, so the instruction is consistent. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
